title: Four Companies Reported $539 Billion in Capex. NVIDIA Booked $278 Billion. The Filings Don't Connect Them.
description: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta reported about $539 billion of capital spending for calendar Q3 2025 through Q2 2026. NVIDIA's Data Center revenue for the fiscal quarters ending roughly a month later was about $278 billion. This video sets the two beside each other, quarter by quarter, and explains what the filings do and don't say: the capex measures differ by company (finance leases, net of proceeds, cash purchases), the ratios compare scale rather than measuring payments to NVIDIA or NVIDIA's share of that spending, and company forecasts are separated from reported results. Sources are SEC filings, earnings releases and earnings-call remarks; call remarks are labeled. No investment recommendation is made.

4.narration: NVIDIA booked 278 billion. No filing says how much of that capex went to NVIDIA. The ratio is a comparison, not a share.

6.narration: NVIDIA's books show about 216 billion of revenue in its fiscal 2026, almost all of it from its Data Center platform.

7.narration: That platform reported about 194 billion, up from about 115 billion a year earlier, split between compute and networking.

11.narration: That filing put the hyperscaler category at roughly half of data center sales. A later filing recast the category; its numbers imply about 57 percent.

19.narration: Together, that spending came to roughly 112.5 billion. NVIDIA's Data Center revenue was 51.2 billion in its October quarter.

59.narration: NVIDIA guided its next quarter to 108 billion of revenue, plus or minus 2 percent. Every budget shown here was revised this year.

60.narration: A supplier's outlook rests on customer budgets rewritten quarter by quarter. The filings give the balances. They do not say who financed what.
